title: rework-sse-timestamping-and-unambiguous-delimiter-handling
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Stabilize SSE stream reassembly by introducing per-fragment monotonic timestamps and deterministic delimiter normalization. Addresses rare partial-JSON emission and out-of-order event delivery under heavy backpressure. No public API changes.
description:
Motivation: In long-lived SSE connections we continue to see glitches where a delimiter ("

") or event boundary can be interpreted inconsistently across proxies and our client reassembly, producing partial JSON objects or ordering anomalies when packetization aligns with UTF-8 multi-byte boundaries. This PR reworks how we mark and reassemble fragments to make consumer-side reassembly deterministic even when fragments arrive out of logical order or are split on codepoint boundaries.

What this changes: adds a compact per-fragment monotonic timestamp + seq-offset header emitted by the server runtime, applies a normalization pass that collapses ambiguous delimiter runs into a canonical marker before parsing, and hardens the stream parser to accept and reorder within a short, bounded window using timestamps rather than relying solely on arrival ordering. Also instruments a new set of observability metrics for fragment reorder, delimiter-normalization rate, and reassembly retries.

Checklist:
- [x] Reassembly algorithm with timestamp window and idempotent normalization implemented in runtime stream layer
- [x] Backwards-compatible framing header (optional; parser tolerates both old and new framing)
- [x] Unit tests covering UTF-8 split boundaries and proxy-induced chunk reordering
- [x] Integration test against nginx proxy emulation and node/ts client harness
- [x] Added metrics and dashboards for fragment reordering and normalization events
- [x] Release note entry prepared

Rollout plan: feature gated by runtime flag (sse.fragment_ts=on). Default enabled in canary and dedicated, monitor metrics for 72h, then flip global flag. If regressions observed, runtime will fall back to legacy framing for affected connections and emit a debug trace to support.

Backward compatibility: The framing header is optional and ignored by older clients. Normalization step is idempotent and only affects internal stream boundary resolution; it does not mutate payload content outside of delimiting sequences.

Related work: Builds on ENG-1209 (previous delimiter fixes) but differs by moving to timestamp/small-offset ordering rather than larger sequence windows. Linked Linear items: ENG-1347, ENG-1372. Support ticket SUP-8821 repro included in tests.

@@ -1,3 +1,28 @@
+// Normalize runs of delimiters that could be ambiguous across proxies.
+func NormalizeDelimiters(b []byte) []byte {
+ // collapse CRLF/
 sequences into canonical
+ return bytes.ReplaceAll(b, []byte{0x0D,0x0A,0x0A}, []byte{0x0A,0x0A})
+}
review_comments: Connor Lee: Nice approach. Two questions: (1) how does this behave with replayed fragments from proxies that buffer and retransmit? (2) Do we need an escape if payload legitimately contains the delimiter sequence?

Asha Patel: For (1) we use a short monotonic window (300ms by default) and also detect replays by identical fragment payload+seq checksum; replayed fragments outside the window are treated as duplicates and dropped. For (2) delimiter normalization only runs on the stream framing layer before payload parsing and respects explicit "data:" event prefixes; we added tests for payloads with embedded delimiter-like sequences.
Maya Singh: Can you add a telemetry tag to connect fragment reorders back to connection id and upstream proxy?
Asha Patel: Added r.conn_id tag to fragment_reorder metric and a debug trace emitted when reorder_count > 3 in a minute.
merge_summary: Squash-merged and enabled feature flag in canary pool. No regressions observed in canary (72h).
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: subtle regressions in client parsers that assume strict arrival ordering. Mitigation: feature gated rollout, server emits compatibility header and falls back to legacy mode when client signals incompatibility, added extensive integration tests and canary monitoring. Support playbook updated.
notes_for_support: If customers report truncated JSON in streams, check fragment_reorder and normalization_rate. Toggle runtime flag sse.fragment_ts=off to restore legacy behavior while we collect traces.
changelog_entry: Runtime: stabilize SSE framing using fragment timestamps and delimiter normalization (canary first, rollouts configurable).
